comment: Grok episode, recorded 2026-10-28 on SpecWithCode 1.0.111 (take r2-13). Times in seconds; segments are [sourceStart, sourceEnd, rate] in take.mp4 (cue time = video time; syncOffset from blackdetect). The take also ran the older Add provider steps after Providers opened (22.5-41 s); 1.0.111 had already turned Grok on, so those seconds are cut and SHOTLIST.json now stops at the Providers list. The coordinator's wait (40 s) and the worker's run (298 s) are speed-ramped.

captions.text: Grok in SpecWithCode: one task, planned, built and reviewed.
In your repo, run `specweave init` with the generic adapter.
It adds `AGENTS.md` and seven SpecWeave skills.
Then run `grok --trust` once, so Grok loads them.
Open SpecWithCode and set this Mac up as your main machine.
Grok isn't in the first-run list, so continue past it.
Grok signs in with its own CLI.
In Settings, Providers, SpecWithCode has already turned Grok on, because its CLI is signed in.
Add the repo: the plus next to Projects, Local folder, then its path.
The project opens on its coordinator, and the model picker already shows Grok.
Set Full access for this demo, describe the change, and send it.
The coordinator hands the work to a new thread.
The thread plans increment 1: acceptance criteria and one task with its test.
Then it changes the code and runs that test.
A task is done only when its test passes.
Open the thread to review it: the summary,
the verification and review reports, and every changed file in Open diff.
Next, run the same task with another agent.
